emphasis_summary: IK India's catalog is overwhelmingly oriented toward Agentic AI engineering for transitioning professionals, paired with FAANG/Tier-1 interview prep. Its deepest, most repeated coverage is the agentic application stack: multi-agent orchestration (planner-executor-critic, router, supervisor-worker, HITL), RAG/Agentic RAG/Hybrid Retrieval, MCP/A2A protocols, agent evaluation (LLM-as-Judge, retrieval metrics), guardrails/safety, fine-tuning (LoRA/PEFT/QLoRA), and deployment to FastAPI/Docker/Kubernetes/AWS — taught identically across 13 EdgeUp engineering tracks and reinforced in the PwC accelerator (which adds enterprise depth: GraphRAG, RBAC, audit trails, real regulated datasets). It strongly covers the role archetypes of Agentic AI Engineer, RAG Engineer, GenAI-enabled domain engineer (backend/fullstack/frontend/mobile/data/cloud/security/devops/embedded), AI/ML Architect, and the leadership/no-code lane (AI PM, TPM, EM, ML Leader). Classic ML, deep learning, computer vision, time-series and full MLOps live almost entirely in two courses (Flagship ML for Leaders, and the DS/ML EdgeUp tracks) rather than across the catalog. The clear orientation is: applied, production-leaning agentic AI + interview readiness for mid-career engineers and leaders, with India/enterprise framing.
possible_blindspots: Production LLMOps / agent operations at scale — observability, evaluation and deployment are taught, but dedicated LLMOps (CI/CD for prompts/models, A/B rollout of agents, online eval harnesses, cost/usage governance at fleet scale) appears thin outside the Flagship ML MLOps specialization. HYPOTHESIS to test vs market demand.

Classic ML / Deep Learning breadth — supervised/unsupervised ML, CV, RL and time-series are concentrated in only ~2-3 courses (Flagship ML, DS, ML Engineers, DA); most agentic tracks teach little-to-no classical modeling. May be a gap if market demand for pure ML/DL roles is high.
Computer Vision as a standalone career track — CV appears only as a tag in ML/DS/PM courses (YOLO/ResNet/U-Net in Flagship ML); no dedicated CV engineer pathway. HYPOTHESIS.

Data Engineering depth for AI — one EdgeUp DE track covers ETL/Spark/Kafka/dbt/Snowflake, but feature stores, real-time ML data infra, and vector-data-at-scale engineering may be underweight relative to demand.

AI Safety / Governance / Responsible AI depth — present as guardrails, PII, prompt-injection and (in PM/TPM/PwC) governance/RBAC/audit, but no dedicated AI governance, red-teaming, model-risk, or AI-policy/compliance specialist track. HYPOTHESIS.

Model/research-level skills — pre-training, model architecture research, large-scale distributed training, and novel fine-tuning research are largely absent (only applied fine-tuning + transformers theory in Flagship ML). Likely intentional given applied focus; flag if 'AI Research Engineer' roles surface in market data.

Pure AI Product Management vs PM-with-agentic-skills — PM/TPM tracks are strong on agentic product design but it is unclear how deeply they cover AI-specific product strategy, model selection economics, and data/eval strategy as a standalone AI PM discipline.

Emerging roles potentially uncovered — 'AI Evaluation/Eval Engineer', 'Prompt Engineer' as a standalone role, 'AI Red Team / Security Researcher', 'AI Solutions/Forward-Deployed Engineer', and 'AI Infrastructure/Inference-serving Engineer' are touched as skills but not positioned as named role outcomes. Test these titles explicitly against scraped market roles.
